The story is a cohesive, well-crafted slice-of-life piece where every element works together to create a unified whole. It follows a clear, logical progression: waiting at the dock, boarding the three distinct passengers, and making the crossing through the fog. Each interaction—from the chatty regular, Frau Wulf, to the quiet repairman and the rushed schoolboy—serves to establish the rhythm of Ilse’s routine and her stoic, grounded character. The motifs of the fog, the cable, and knowing things without needing to see them (the opposite shore, the faded schedule, the caller on the vibrating phone) are woven seamlessly throughout the narrative, tying the beginning directly to the quiet, satisfying ending as the far bank finally emerges from the mist.
